q: Chaitin's Ω (halting probability) is defined as Ω = ∑_{U(p) halts} 2^{-|p|}. Ω is:
opts: A well-defined real in [0,1] that is Martin-Löf random and encodes the halting problem
Equal to 1/2 for all universal machines
exp: Ω is the probability that a random program halts. It is well-defined and between 0 and 1. Its binary expansion encodes the halting problem: knowing the first n bits of Ω lets one decide which programs of length ≤n halt. Ω is Martin-Löf random — maximally incompressible.
